paras: The lynching of Archie Wright was the reported killing of a man named Archie Wright at Vicksburg, Mississippi, in or shortly before early October 1881. He was said to have been lynched for "offering indignities to respectable young ladies," and the event is known only from a one-line news brief.

According to the brief, Wright was lynched at Vicksburg over the accusation that he had offered "indignities" to young women described as "respectable." The item gives no date, names no one who took part, and does not say how he was killed, where in or near the town it happened, or whether he had been arrested. It also does not state Wright's race or that of the young women.
No report of an inquest, arrests or any official response appears in the coverage.

The lynching reached print in the South Kentuckian of Hopkinsville, Kentucky, on 4 October 1881, as one sentence in a "General News" column of short telegraphic items. There it ran between a report of a storm at Madison, Nebraska, and a note about a granddaughter of Thomas Jefferson visiting the White House, with no headline or comment of its own. The same column noted that two men accused of murder "were lynched at Oconto, Wis.," in the same flat style.

The brief stated the accusation as the reason for the killing, without qualification, and gave the young women's respectability as part of that reason. The coverage contains no account from a Mississippi paper and no second report of the Vicksburg lynching.

A2 says Wright 'was lynched' for an alleged offense against young women, which reports an extralegal killing under a pretext of punishment, but the one-line item names no mob, number of attackers, method or date, and no second report confirms it.
Only one brief in a Kentucky weekly's wire-news column reports the Vicksburg lynching (A2); no Mississippi or other report was found.

record_check.dossier: The report does not give Archie Wright's race; one person killed, race not stated.
Date not stated; reported 1881-10-04 among briefs from roughly the previous week, so the lynching took place on or before 4 October, possibly in late September.
The report names only Vicksburg, Miss.; no county is given.
Probable lynching: the report calls it a lynching for an alleged offense, but gives no group, size or method.

set_aside: Macon Telegraph and Messenger special from Blakely, Ga., Sept. 29: about a dozen masked men shot Zandy Wright, a Black jail prisoner serving a sentence for hog stealing; a different place, name and charge.
Brief: Andy Wright, a Black prisoner in the jail at Blakely, Ga., taken out and lynched 'Sunday morning'; the Blakely killing, not Vicksburg.
